designSummary: Two-arm pragmatic trial with individual allocation stratified by centre; binary primary outcome at 24 weeks.
sampleSize: With 38 percent attending two thirds of sessions under usual classes and a smallest worthwhile difference of 12 percentage points (to 50 percent), 80 percent power at two-sided alpha 0.05 needs about 268 participants per arm, 536 in total. Allowing 10 percent who consent but never attend a class after allocation gives about 596. At about 43 new participants a month, recruitment takes about 14 months of 2027 and early 2028 intakes. Falls: with about 0.9 falls per person-year, the trial cannot detect a plausible reduction and falls are reported with a rate ratio and its interval, not tested.
primaryAnalysis: Logistic regression of attendance at two thirds of sessions on arm, adjusted for centre and age group, intention to treat; the risk difference with its 95 percent confidence interval is reported alongside the odds ratio.
secondaryAnalysis: Home exercise days by linear regression at weeks 12 and 24; falls as a rate ratio from negative binomial regression with its interval; delivery proportions; injuries and pain flares described by arm.
missingData: Attendance is complete from registers; missing phone checks and falls calendars are handled by multiple imputation under missing at random, with a sensitivity analysis assuming worse outcomes for non-responders.
multiplicity: One primary outcome; secondary outcomes reported with intervals and labelled as secondary.
software: R; the statistical analysis plan archived before the first allocation.
overfittingGuards: Two adjustment variables fixed in advance
No subgroup analyses beyond sex and phone ownership, both pre-specified
summary: About 268 participants per arm for a 12-point difference in attendance; falls descriptive.
